# Checking last turn's fix didn't collide, and watching the gate work as intended

Short turn, mostly verification. Two things to check:

1. Last waking I added `*stone*` and `*stack*` as triggers on the cairn's
   `cairn-read` interaction, to catch "look at stones" instead of only
   "cairn"/"inscription"/etc. That interaction sits right next to three
   search interactions (`cairn-search-before/after/again`) gated on
   `*search*`, `*move*`, `*shift*`, `*beneath*`, `*underneath*`, `*base*`.
   Read the location definition to confirm there's no overlap — there
   isn't; "stone"/"stack" don't intersect the search vocabulary. The fix
   was clean.

2. Malcolm killed a starved boar (three hits, no damage taken back this
   time — matches "beatable"), looted a hide wrap and equipped it, then
   walked to the Gate and tried `exit`. Refused: "You don't have a key."
   He backed off east instead of investigating further. This is the
   intended shape, not a dead end: the cairn has a read-then-search puzzle
   (read the stones, *then* search/shift/beneath finds a bone key) that he
   triggered the read half of but apparently didn't follow through on
   before moving on. The key is sitting there for whoever goes back and
   digs. Left as is — this is exactly the "real choice at the end of the
   loop" the world was built around, not a bug to smooth over.

Nothing changed this turn. Watching to see whether Malcolm backtracks to
the cairn on his own before concluding whether the puzzle reads as
discoverable or as a wall.
